entries.title: fd
entries.summary: File descriptors: the integers that identify open files.
entries.description: A descriptor is a non-negative integer that indexes a per-process table of open files. Calls that create one (`open`, `creat`, `dup`) return the LOWEST unused number; `dup2` lets you choose it. Each `open` of a file creates a new open-file entry with its own position; `dup` and `dup2` create another descriptor for the SAME entry, so the position is shared. Errors return -1 and set `errno`; a valid descriptor is never negative.

entries.title: open
entries.summary: Open or create a file and get a descriptor.
entries.syntax:
int open(const char *path, int flags);
int open(const char *path, int flags, mode_t mode);
entries.description: Exactly one access mode plus any extra flags joined with `|`. `mode` (permissions of a new file) is needed with `O_CREAT` and ignored otherwise; the real permissions are `mode & ~umask`. Returns the descriptor or -1.

details.name: O_CREAT
details.text: create the file if it does not exist (needs `mode`)

details.name: O_TRUNC
details.text: empty the file if it exists

details.name: O_APPEND
details.text: every write goes to the end

details.name: O_EXCL
details.text: with O_CREAT: fail if the file already exists
the same permissions as an octal number: owner rw, group r, others r

entries.example:
int fd = open("log.txt", O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_APPEND, 0644);
if (fd < 0) { perror("log.txt"); return 1; }

entries.title: creat
entries.summary: Create (or empty) a file and open it for writing.
entries.description: Exactly `open(path, O_WRONLY | O_CREAT | O_TRUNC, mode)`. Returns the descriptor or -1.

entries.title: read
entries.syntax: ssize_t read(int fd, void *buf, size_t count);
entries.description: Returns the number of bytes read (possibly LESS than `count`), 0 at the end of the file, or -1 on error. The file position advances by the amount read.
mistakes: Treating a short read as the end of the file: only 0 means that.
Declaring the result as `int` or `size_t`: it must be signed (`ssize_t`).

entries.title: write
entries.syntax: ssize_t write(int fd, const void *buf, size_t count);
entries.description: Returns the number of bytes written, which can be less than `count` (for example after a signal): check it. Returns -1 on error. Write exactly what you read: `write(out, buf, n)` with `n` the return value of `read`.
mistakes: Writing `sizeof buf` bytes instead of the bytes actually read.

entries.title: lseek
entries.summary: Change the position of a descriptor.
entries.syntax: off_t lseek(int fd, off_t offset, int whence);
entries.description: Returns the new position from the start of the file, or -1. `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END)` returns the file size; `lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_CUR)` the current position.
entries.example:
off_t size = lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_END);
lseek(fd, 0, SEEK_SET);   /* back to the start */

entries.title: close
entries.description: Returns 0 on success, -1 on error. The number becomes free and may be reused by the next `open`. A process has a limited number of descriptors: close what you open.

entries.title: dup
entries.summary: Copy a descriptor into the lowest free number.
entries.description: The new descriptor refers to the same open file: the same position and flags. Returns the new descriptor or -1.
entries.example: int copy = dup(1);   /* another way to write on stdout */
mistakes: Expecting the copies to have independent positions.

entries.title: dup2
entries.summary: Make newfd a copy of oldfd (closing newfd first); the basis of redirection.
entries.description: If `newfd` was open it is closed first; if `oldfd == newfd` nothing happens. Both descriptors then share the same position. Returns `newfd` or -1.

details.name: redirect stdout to a file
details.text: open the file, `dup2(fd, STDOUT_FILENO)`, `close(fd)`; later `printf` output goes to the file (flush stdio first)

mistakes: Forgetting to flush the stdio buffers before redirecting.

entries.title: access
entries.summary: Test whether the file exists or you may read, write or execute it.
entries.description: Returns 0 if the access is allowed, -1 otherwise (see `errno`). `mode` is `F_OK` (exists), or `R_OK`, `W_OK`, `X_OK` joined with `|`.

details.name: X_OK
details.text: may execute (or search, for a directory)

mistakes: Using it to 'check, then open': the file can change in between; just try `open` and check the result.
